statement: Define and prove the critical-placement convergence evaluator: for a critical system partition, spread means the required replica count on that many DISTINCT nodes each holding a quorum-voting partition replica, not a logical replica count that three seed-local replicas already satisfy. This slice defines the invariant and its evaluator only; wiring it into the formation barrier and TRAFFIC_READY is a later slice.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

The critical partition set is read from CRITICAL_SYSTEM_PARTITION_IDS (system-partition-classification.js), the required replica count from getInitialReplicaIds (system-table-schemas-constants.js), the voter test from isVoterRaftRole (raft/replica-voter-readiness.js), and the service type from SERVICE_TYPE. The evaluator re-derives none of them locally and hardcodes no replication factor or role list.

Convergence for a critical partition is the count of DISTINCT node IDs each holding an active, quorum-voting partition replica of THAT partition, and must be >= the required replica count. Three replicas on one node is not converged; learners and non-partition services are not eligible capacity; rows for another partition never contribute.

The answer is invariant under ambient mutation of Array, Object, Set and String prototypes, including Set.prototype.forEach and Set.prototype.values: Sets are drained through a captured iterator and every row field is read through an own-property descriptor.

The evaluator is a pure projection over supplied rows: it mints no readiness verdict, no lifecycle transition and no cluster-ACTIVE or READY answer, and nothing derives ACTIVE or READY from nodes.status, publication counts, or coverage.
Absent, empty or unreadable placement evidence is NOT converged, with a typed reason; absence is never treated as satisfaction and is never skipped.

No existing readiness, barrier, routing or lifecycle behaviour changes in this Quest; nothing yet consumes the evaluator; system-table creation keeps its seed-local initial representation; ratchet baselines are not raised.

Every guard the evaluator relies on has a receipt that reds when that guard is removed: partition_id, voter role, service type, and the captured Set iterator were each verified by mutation to flip exactly one receipt red. A receipt that cannot fail is not evidence.
classification-vocabulary-unchanged lives in a test file that does NOT import the evaluator, so it stays green when the evaluator is absent and reds only on real vocabulary drift.
